RFO:

BR04.HKG05 experienced a service degradation/failure due to a combination of aging hardware and outdated software. The existing Cisco ASR9K platform is at its lifecycle limit and struggles with modern traffic scale requirements. The router was running an outdated software version (XR6.5.3 SP2) which lacked critical stability patches found in newer Service Packs (SP5). The legacy hardware could no longer reliably sustain network demands in its current state.
Custom field (Fix):
Short term solution: A normal Change Management Request (CMR) has been initiated to upgrade br04.hkg05 from XR6.5.3 SP2 to XR6.5.3 SP5. This will apply critical service packs to stabilize the node temporarily. IPE to provide the exact date of the CMR.

Permanent solution: Engineering is discussing  the complete decommissioning of the EOL ASR9K router br04.hkg05. All affected customer circuits will be migrated to next-generation, high-capacity Border Routers (Cisco NCS55A1 and NCS57B1) in HKG05. This will permanently resolve the capacity and stability constraints. IPE and TAC will work together to migrate the services pending date of the activity (~1 to 2 months).
